verdict: A clean, consistent small pause card, but its title "press a" is the wrong content for a pause menu, and the card is tiny and floats in an empty black screen with no game behind it.

findings.what: The title reads "press a", which is a pad-lost prompt and not a pause or menu title. Everything else on the card is a pause menu (resume, settings, end run). The player gets a conflicting message, and it is the first thing the eye reads.
findings.fix: Use one state per screen. Either title the card "paused" with the pad prompt as a small --fs-label line under it, or show a dedicated pad-lost card with a 56px hero prompt like "press a" and no menu buttons.

findings.what: The screen is a flat #0b0c0d void with a 480x485 card in the middle. There is no scrim over the game, no blurred raid behind it, and no player context. It reads as a debug page, not a pause over a live raid. The identity score is low.
findings.fix: Dim the raid frame with --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80). Add the run state (timer, sector) as quiet --tx-2 --fs-label text. Optionally scale the card up to about 560px wide.

findings.what: The hierarchy is correct (lime resume on top), but the secondary buttons are all identical and the tail is crowded. Report a problem, feedback and what's new are three low-value actions with the same weight as settings. Report a problem and feedback also overlap in purpose, which breaks the one-control-per-job rule.
findings.fix: Keep resume, settings and end run. Merge feedback and report a problem into one "feedback" button, and move what's new into settings or the title screen.

findings.what: The red label has no button shape, so it does not look pressable. It also has no visible pad focus state, and it is the only destructive action. It is 20px text in red #e5482f on a dark panel, which is borderline contrast, and it is separated by an uneven gap (about 44px below the row above versus 16px between buttons).
findings.fix: Give it a 56px high ghost button with a 1px --danger border, spaced 16px like the others. Add a confirm step before the run ends. Keep the 3px lime focus bar on it when focused.

findings.what: Only resume shows focus, as a flat lime fill. The unfocused buttons have no glyph and no pad prompt, so pad users get no hint of what the nav buttons do. A filled lime button is also the primary-action style, so the focus style and the primary style are the same, which blurs the system.
findings.fix: Show focus as a lime 2px border and a 3px left bar with --ui-raised fill. Keep the filled lime only for the one primary action. Add a small pad-button glyph in the footer.

findings.what: The top-left 36px accent tab is dim olive, not --acc, so it looks like a rendering fault. The X is a thin light-grey glyph about 26px wide with no hit box, and it is not vertically centred on the title baseline (title at y~350, X at y~346).
findings.fix: Draw the accent tab in full --acc, 2px high, aligned on the card's left edge. Make the X a 40px square hit area centred on the title row, with a 2px stroke in --tx-1.

findings.what: The card has 40px side padding and 24px of empty space under end run. Its bottom padding does not match the 24px panel padding in the guide, and the text is only 20px on a 1080 screen read from a couch. Overall the card is small and the menu is dense in the middle with an empty screen around it.
findings.fix: Use 24px padding on all sides, set the button height to 56px with 16px gaps, and raise the card to about 560px wide so it reads from across the room.
